Role: Marketing Director
Industry: Museums and Institutions
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 4
Pros: It is hard to really list all of the things. I think the biggest is that it has tools that help me take an overwhelming amount of work and make sense of it. And it does it in a way that is a dopamine rush for me. It feels really good to use Asana and it feels even better that using it means that I'm gaining more and more control over my work/life balance. Through the years of using it, I have found that keeping track of tasks helps me report better but it also helps me have a better understanding of my workflow. It also made onboarding a new assistant into my department SO simple. I was able to take tasks I assigned to myself and give them to her. While it does cost to use Asana, for myself I find it to be very worth it.
Cons: There are a couple. The biggest is that it is that I have not been able to secure organizational buy in. [truncated]

Role: Owner
Industry: Farming
Company size: Self-employed
Time used: Less than 6 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Asana has a lot of feature to collab with others
Cons: Less popular so it’s hard to get some tutorial sources

Role: Software Engineer
Industry: Information Technology and Services
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 4
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Asana is great project management software for tracking the progress of tasks and collaborating with other team members on a project. It is simple to use and has perfected its core functionality. It's suitable for teams or users who want to get organized and productive without unnecessary complexity.
Cons: It has fewer features compared to some of its alternatives and the pricing is on the higher side.
Comments: My overall experience with Asana has been very positive. The interface is clean and has the essential features.

Role: Owner and Managing Director
Industry: Market Research
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: Less than 6 months
Overall rating: 3
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Offers multiple ways to view projects: List, Board (Kanban), Timeline (Gantt), and Calendar views, catering to different team preferences
Cons: Critical features like Timeline view and custom fields are locked behind premium tiers.
Comments: Paid plans start at $10+/user/month (billed annually), which can be expensive for small teams.

Role: E-Commerce Manager
Industry: Retail
Company size: 51-200 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: I love how easy it is to submit and track tasks across the platform with different teams.
Cons: N/A, I've had nothing but positive experiences with the product so far.

Role: Manager of Registration Support
Industry: Professional Training & Coaching
Company size: 51-200 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 4
Ease-of-use rating: 4
Pros: They way in which you can create easily accessible projects and tasks within to make collaboration between departments visible. The added option to create subtasks in a single task that make following up cohesive, is also appreciated.
Cons: Been a user for two years and still struggle to find created and assigned tasks to others easily. Creating the tasks is not an issue when you have it open, but there is lack of streamlined searching functions (or personal folder views, bookmarks that doesn’t require a prior notification) to make individual priorities top of your list.
Comments: Overall I like it. Call it that I grew accustomed to it maybe, so I don’t really see myself using another service unless there’s another one out there that does the same on steroids. They rarely deploy updates that favor [truncated]

Role: Psychologist
Industry: Health, Wellness and Fitness
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Asana is a nimble tool for coordination across multiple projects, staff, and tasks. It is a quick-to-learn platform.
Cons: Like all project management tools, there is a small learning curve with Asana, but the user-friendly features have improved over time.

Role: Property Developer
Industry: Real Estate
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Love using Asana for it efficiency in managing projects for each property I handle .I use tasks,sections and milestones to track every stages and all times all projects are successful before deadlines. Assigning tasks to team members, set due dates and attaching file is easy and fast.Availability of different formats of viewing tasks eg list,Kanban,Gannt chart,tables etc.Many automations of repetitive that saves time and help to manage both multiple tasks and complex worlflows.
Cons: I'm daily user of Asna and I can it require training for new beginners because it offer alot of features ,views and options.
Comments: Overall Asana keep task management and project flowing smoothly.Many automations available saves time on repetitive work and improves efficient.

Role: Virtual Assistant
Industry: Real Estate
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: I like how user friendly it is! Also, I can create lots of projects and customize each one of them!
Cons: One thing maybe is that I cannot archive a project if I'm not the one who created it.
Comments: Overall, I believe it is one of the best project/work management tool out there.

Role: graphic designer
Industry: Marketing and Advertising
Company size: 1-10 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 4
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: I liked Asana because it was easy to separate tasks into different folders and prioritize tasks by urgency and due dates. Easy to share with the team. Easy to track find older tasks and view comments etc.
Cons: Probably the level of integration with other software. There is a little bit of limit but it definitely worth using and keep track of tasks.
Comments: It was straightforward to learn as a first-time user. The interface is not overcomplicating itself and I love it!
Reasons for switching: I moved the company and our company uses function point
Switched from: Function Point

Role: Account Manager
Industry: Marketing and Advertising
Company size: 51-200 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 3
Ease-of-use rating: 3
Pros: It's a platform with the capabilities to build large and long term projects.
Cons: I want an easier UI/UX for team members to see their task load and manage their needs. It's very glitching when trying to duplicate and use large templates.
Comments: Medium - just want better visualization and maybe an option for a less technical UI/UX setup.

Role: Digital Marketer - SEO
Industry: Education Management
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: Less than 6 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Here I can plan my project on monthly basis, schedule my daily tasks and track the performance. I can even check what my colleagues are working on plan the tasks accordingly.It gives an insight into where our project is heading.Can manage all the tasks and projects at one place.A lot of customizations and reports, I can even check the project performance by gantt charts and that actually helps a lot in reporting.Can easily communicate with colleagues.Ability to assign tasks.
Cons: It has a lot many features so sometimes it becomes messy to look over all the things. Rest its a great tool for project management.
Comments: Overall it improves my efficiency and gives me the ability to schedule my project along with reporting and analysis.

Role: Director
Industry: Information Technology and Services
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: It was very fast to set up for our group of ten people. The person they sent to teach us was relentless and so everybody eventually figured it out. Connecting to Slack wasn’t as bad of an experience as I thought it would be either.
Cons: The entire screen will freeze while I’m moving cards around sometimes and it gets me to the point where I want to throw my mouse across the room. I also wish that the proofing add on would allow me to do frame by frame review, as right now, it’s not detailed enough for the video team. There are far too many menus to google through.
Comments: Since it houses the files in one place, I’m not having to dig through 500 emails like a lunatic. I can visually see how much work the creative people are doing and whether or not they are drowning. It’s nice I no longer have to manually repeat the same tasks [truncated]

Role: Account manager y Project manager
Industry: Marketing and Advertising
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: Click Up es una excelente herramienta no solo para project management, sino tambien para mantener todas las comunicaciones del equipo centralizadas.
Cons: Lo que no me gusta, es que aun cuando este linkeado el calendario no marca automaticamente que estas en reunion en tu estado.
Comments: Mi experiencia general es muy buena. Puedo trabajar con todo el equipo, y ademas mostrarle algunas vistas de los proyectos a los clientes
Reasons for choosing: Click up creo que crecio mucho con las nuevas actualizaciones, buscando concentrar gran partes de las herramientas que se usan dia a dia
Alternatives considered: Asana

Role: CEO - Founder
Industry: E-Learning
Company size: Self-employed
Time used: 2+ years
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 4
Pros: I like the fact that all the functionalities as well as the automations have made my worklife and customer follow-up much easier
Cons: Some of the functions are not so clear to me on how to use them, so I may probably be missing out on better things for my company
Comments: I migrated to clikup from trello and it was an amazing decision because of it's visuals, ease to use and the amount of automations and information I can add about my customers, from how much they owe me, to the fact of knowing how many sessions I conduct in a month according to the part of the world they are in.
Reasons for choosing: I still find clickup better, it gives me a broader view of my business and I really like how I can engage with it.
Reasons for switching: Because of the amount of funcitonalities and ease to use, and not to mention the automations!!
Switched from: [truncated]

Role: Infrastructure Analyst
Industry: Law Practice
Company size: 501-1,000 employees
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 5
Pros: It is very organic to use Clickup for collaborating with the team on certain projects
Cons: Can do better in calendar management and notification reminders

Role: Freelance Writer/ Virtual Assistant
Industry: Writing and Editing
Company size: Self-employed
Time used: 6-12 months
Overall rating: 5
Ease-of-use rating: 4
Pros: I love the fact that I can easily access and view my scheduled calendar appointments/meetings. Also, I love the opportunity to collaborate and keep track of tasks (pending, active and concluded).
Cons: I wish the tools was a little more easy to navigate especially if one is a beginner looking for a new or alternative project management tool that is functional and easy.
Comments: I love ClickUp. As a Virtual assistant, it has elevated my career and made things a lot more easier and manageable.

Role: Producer
Industry: Entertainment
Company size: 11-50 employees
Time used: 1-2 years
Overall rating: 3
Ease-of-use rating: 2
Pros: I like the ease of sharing tasks with team members. Very good to keep track of where everyone is at in a project.
Cons: It's pretty difficult to actually figure out how to use all the different capabilities that ClickUp offers. Sometimes it feels like I'm clicking around in circles because I can't find where I'm trying to go.
